summary.suggested: The St. Louis Globe-Democrat reported that Tom Allen was arrested at his Market Street saloon as a fugitive from Kentucky justice over his 1876 fight with Joe Goss, after bondsman W. J. Farrell filed a complaint.

metadata.notes: Masthead: St. Louis Daily Globe-Democrat, Sunday Morning, February 10, 1884, page 9. Arrest was 'yesterday afternoon', February 9.

facts.fact: Allen was arrested at his saloon on Market Street between Sixth and Seventh as a fugitive from Kentucky justice, and released that night on a $2,000 bond to appear before Judge Noonan
places: Market Street between Sixth and Seventh, St. Louis

facts.fact: Allen and Joe Goss were both arrested after their September 1876 fight near Covington, Ky.; Goss was tried and fined $300, while Allen gave a $3,000 bond with Patrick Murphy of Cincinnati and W. J. Farrell and his brother of Covington as sureties
After giving bond in Kentucky, Allen left for England and stayed away about five years
Allen returned to St. Louis from England about a year and a half before February 1884
Allen opened his saloon on Market Street about a year before February 1884

The bond was forfeited and Farrell's property sold to satisfy it; Allen said he had paid Farrell and Murphy $250 each, and a row over Farrell's demand for $200 more led to Farrell's complaint and the arrest
Allen told Farrell he wanted a fair show and would not be bled
facts.quote: all he wanted was a fair show; that he didn't want to be bled, and didn't propose to be, and wanted time

notes: Quote is indirect speech as printed by the paper.
